title: [Prime] Anker 25W USB-C Charger $16.13 (RRP $69.99) Delivered @ AnkerDirect AU via Amazon AU
body:
Deal: [Prime] Anker 25W USB-C Charger $16.13 (RRP $69.99) Delivered @ AnkerDirect AU via Amazon AU

[mmrazz] RRP $70 for something that according to the Camels has not been sold for more than $30 for the past 2 years.
That said, this is basically an all-time low, so does seem like a reasonable deal - but it's definitely not 77% off like they are claiming!
[ozmma] I bought this adapter on Amazon for $12.49 this August. Now they increased the price and calling it 75% off. When I bought it was around 50% off.
[OZKap] Imo better to wait for the Anker 323 which regularly goes on sale for ~$18 https://www.amazon.com.au/Anker-Charger-Compact-iPhone-Inclu…
[tman2020] The Ikea 45w has very good reviews. Can always get their 20w for $6 each.
[wwwsam] @tman2020: Their 20W has relatively high ripple according to my WITRN K2 meter so I probably wouldn't recommend it.
Their 45W and 65W are pretty good.
[Spector1] Anker's products aren't as good as you think they are
[Commodore64] 25 watts? What is this, a charger for ants?
[techno2000] I bought this Belkin 45w for $22.Very compact.
https://amzn.asia/d/01fhphZW
There is also a 30w one for $17
https://amzn.asia/d/0bhu736g
[browser] What so special about this power adapter to justify $70 RRP?
Also, technically this is an AC to DC power supply/adapter, the actual charge management and battery regulation are onboard with the device.
[Erwark] I had 2 of these die within 6 months. Anker was great with replacing them, but I wouldn't buy it again given the chance.
[HeyPapito] Either 45w or 65w should be the minimum you buy - no matter what device you have. 100w if extra spare money laying around.
[superroach] These are still nice for the form factor - you can charge any phone up easily overnight. 45w+ gives you proper PD
